items.title: List comprehension vs generator expression
items.prompt: Explain the difference between a list comprehension and a generator expression. Write one of each that produces the squares of even numbers from 0 to 999, and say when you would pick each one and why.
items.rubric: Mentions laziness vs eager evaluation, memory, single-pass iteration, correct syntax, and a sensible use case for each.

items.title: Mutable default arguments
items.prompt: This function is buggy: def add(item, bucket=[]): bucket.append(item); return bucket. Explain what goes wrong across repeated calls, why Python behaves this way, and rewrite it correctly.
items.rubric: Explains that defaults are evaluated once at definition time, shows shared-state behavior, uses None sentinel in the fix.

items.title: Write a decorator with arguments
items.prompt: Write a decorator retry(times, exceptions) that re-runs the wrapped function up to `times` times if it raises one of `exceptions`, then re-raises. Preserve the wrapped function's name and docstring. Show usage.
items.rubric: Three-level closure or class-based decorator, functools.wraps, loop with re-raise on final attempt, correct exception tuple handling.

items.title: Generators and send()
items.prompt: Write a generator running_average() that yields the running mean of every value sent into it with .send(). Explain how priming works and what StopIteration means for generators.
items.rubric: Uses yield as an expression, handles priming with next(), keeps count and total, explains StopIteration/return value.

items.title: The GIL
items.prompt: What is the Global Interpreter Lock? Explain what it means for CPU-bound and I/O-bound work, and which of threading, multiprocessing, and asyncio you would pick for each, with one sentence of reasoning per choice.
items.rubric: Correctly separates CPU-bound (multiprocessing) from I/O-bound (threads or asyncio), explains the GIL releases on I/O, mentions the 3.13 free-threaded build as optional extra.

items.title: asyncio basics
items.prompt: Write an async function that fetches 20 URLs concurrently with a limit of 5 in flight at once, collects results, and does not let one failure cancel the rest. Use only asyncio primitives in the sketch (you may assume an async fetch(url) exists).
items.rubric: Uses a Semaphore, asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True or TaskGroup with per-task handling, awaits correctly, no blocking calls.

items.title: __slots__, dataclasses and memory
items.prompt: You have 10 million small Point objects with x and y. Compare a plain class, a @dataclass, a @dataclass(slots=True), a namedtuple and a tuple for memory and ergonomics. Which do you pick and why?
items.rubric: Explains per-instance __dict__ cost, what __slots__ removes, immutability and hashing differences, picks slots dataclass or namedtuple with reasoning.

items.title: Context managers
items.prompt: Implement a context manager timer() two ways: as a class with __enter__/__exit__ and with contextlib.contextmanager. It should print elapsed time even if the block raises. Explain the __exit__ return value.
items.rubric: Both forms correct, uses try/finally in the generator form, explains that returning True suppresses the exception.

items.title: Shallow vs deep copy
items.prompt: Given nested = [[1, 2], [3, 4]], show what a = nested, b = list(nested), c = copy.deepcopy(nested) each do when you then run nested[0].append(9). Explain the reference model behind it.
items.rubric: Correct outputs for each, explains names bind to objects, shallow copy shares inner lists.

items.title: Hashing and dict keys
items.prompt: Why can a tuple be a dict key but a list cannot? Write a class whose instances can be used as dict keys and that compares equal by value. What invariant must __eq__ and __hash__ keep?
items.rubric: Mutability vs hashability, implements __eq__ and __hash__ consistently, states equal objects must hash equal.

items.title: LRU cache from scratch
items.prompt: Implement an LRU cache class with get(key) and put(key, value) in O(1) each, without functools.lru_cache. Then say how you would do it in one line with the standard library.
items.rubric: OrderedDict with move_to_end/popitem(last=False) or dict plus doubly linked list, O(1) argument, mentions functools.lru_cache or OrderedDict.

items.title: Exceptions done right
items.prompt: Write a small function that reads a JSON config file and returns a dict, with sensible error handling. Explain when to catch broad exceptions, what exception chaining (raise ... from ...) does, and why bare except is bad.
items.rubric: Catches specific exceptions, uses from for chaining, explains bare except swallowing KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, uses with for the file.

items.title: Type hints and Protocols
items.prompt: Write a Protocol for anything that has a .close() method, a function that accepts that protocol, and show it works with an object that never imports your Protocol. Explain structural vs nominal typing in one paragraph.
items.rubric: typing.Protocol usage, duck typing explanation, optional runtime_checkable mention, Optional/Union correctness.

items.title: Sorting with keys
items.prompt: Sort a list of (name, dept, salary) tuples by dept ascending then salary descending in one call. Explain why Python's sort is stable and why that matters here. What is the complexity?
items.rubric: key= with a tuple and negation or two stable sorts, stability explanation, O(n log n).

items.title: itertools in practice
items.prompt: Using itertools, write: (a) chunk an iterable into groups of n, (b) all pairs from a list, (c) group a sorted list of records by a key. Explain why groupby needs sorted input.
items.rubric: islice or batched, combinations, groupby with sorted input, explains groupby only groups consecutive runs.

items.title: String building performance
items.prompt: Compare building a large string with += in a loop versus ''.join(). Explain the complexity of each and show how you would measure it with timeit.
items.rubric: Quadratic vs linear, immutability of str, timeit usage.

items.title: Descriptors and properties
items.prompt: Implement a Positive descriptor that validates numbers are > 0 on assignment, use it for two attributes on a class, and explain how @property relates to the descriptor protocol.
items.rubric: __set_name__, __get__, __set__ implemented, per-instance storage, explains property is a descriptor.

items.title: Metaclasses vs __init_subclass__
items.prompt: You want every subclass of Plugin to auto-register itself in a registry dict. Show two ways: __init_subclass__ and a metaclass. Which would you ship and why?
items.rubric: Both implementations correct, recommends __init_subclass__ for simplicity, explains when a metaclass is actually needed.

items.title: Closures and late binding
items.prompt: Explain the output of: fs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]; print([f() for f in fs]). Fix it two ways. What does nonlocal do?
items.rubric: Prints [2, 2, 2], explains late binding, fixes via default arg and functools.partial or a factory, explains nonlocal.

items.title: Logging in a service
items.prompt: Set up logging for a small service: module-level loggers, a JSON formatter, INFO to stdout, and a way to add request_id to every line without passing it around. Explain why you never use print in production code.
items.rubric: logging.getLogger(__name__), handler/formatter setup, contextvars or LoggerAdapter/Filter for request_id, reasons against print.

items.title: Unit testing with pytest
items.prompt: Write pytest tests for a function parse_duration('1h30m') -> 5400 including parametrized cases and an invalid-input case. Show how you would mock time.time() in a test of a retry helper.
items.rubric: @pytest.mark.parametrize, pytest.raises, monkeypatch or unittest.mock.patch, clear naming.

items.title: Reading a huge file
items.prompt: Count how many lines in a 50 GB log file contain the word ERROR, without loading the file into memory. Then say how you would parallelize it across cores.
items.rubric: Iterates the file object line by line, mentions buffering, multiprocessing with chunked offsets or splitting the file.

items.title: *args, **kwargs and keyword-only
items.prompt: Explain the signature def f(a, b, /, c, *, d, **kw). Which arguments are positional-only, keyword-only, and why would you design a function that way?
items.rubric: Correct reading of / and *, gives API-stability and readability reasons.

items.title: Dataclass ordering and frozen
items.prompt: Write a frozen, orderable dataclass Version(major, minor, patch) that parses from 'v1.2.3' via a classmethod and sorts correctly. Explain what frozen=True changes.
items.rubric: order=True, frozen=True, classmethod parser, explains immutability and hashability.

items.title: Memory profiling and references
items.prompt: A long-running worker's memory keeps growing. Describe how you would find the leak in Python: tools, what reference cycles and __del__ have to do with it, and two common causes in real code.
items.rubric: tracemalloc or objgraph, gc module, cycles with __del__, caches without bounds, closures holding references, global lists.

items.title: Packaging and virtual environments
items.prompt: Explain the difference between a virtual environment, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml and a lock file. What goes in each and why does a lock file matter for a service you deploy?
items.rubric: Isolation, direct deps vs pinned transitive deps, reproducible builds.

items.title: Producer-consumer with queues
items.prompt: Implement a producer-consumer pipeline with threading and queue.Queue: 1 producer, 4 consumers, clean shutdown with a sentinel, and backpressure via maxsize. Explain why queue.Queue is safe to share.
items.rubric: Daemon threads or join, sentinel per consumer, maxsize for backpressure, task_done/join, explains internal locking.

items.title: Iterating dicts safely
items.prompt: What happens if you delete keys from a dict while iterating over it? Show the error, two safe patterns, and explain dict ordering guarantees in modern Python.
items.rubric: RuntimeError, iterate over list(d) or build a new dict/comprehension, insertion order since 3.7.

items.title: Regular expressions
items.prompt: Write a regex that extracts (method, path, status) from an nginx access log line, compile it once, and explain greedy vs non-greedy and when re is the wrong tool.
items.rubric: Named groups, re.compile at module level, greedy/non-greedy explanation, mentions parsing libraries for structured formats.

items.title: Design a small CLI
items.prompt: Sketch a CLI tool `dedupe FILE --key email` using argparse: subcommand-free, with a dry-run flag, exit codes, and stderr for errors. Explain how you would make it testable.
items.rubric: argparse setup, sys.exit codes, separates parsing from logic for tests, uses stderr correctly.
